backlog.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum from 0.85 at step 0 to 0.95 by about step 300 with a linear schedule, then hold at 0.95. Change only the momentum schedule inside the Muon update, keeping all LRs and betas as they are.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup

backlog.spec: Reduce the Newton-Schulz orthogonalization in Muon from 5 iterations to 3 to free wall-clock time for more optimizer steps within the fixed 300 s budget. Keep the quintic coefficients and everything else unchanged, then check whether the extra steps outweigh the less accurate orthogonalization.
backlog.title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations for Muon

backlog.spec: Lower MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.03 to test whether the Muon step size is too aggressive for this short run. Leave all other hyperparameters fixed so the comparison isolates the matrix learning rate.
backlog.title: Matrix LR sweep lower

backlog.spec: Give the embedding (and lm_head) Adam group betas of (0.9, 0.99) while keeping ADAM_BETAS = (0.8, 0.95) for the scalar parameters. Only the per-group betas change, so the effect on the embedding optimizer is isolated.
backlog.title: Embedding Adam betas

backlog.spec: Replace the cautious (sign-agreement masked) weight decay in Muon with standard decoupled weight decay applied to every matrix update, using WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.2 scaled by the current LR. Keep the rest of the Muon update unchanged.
backlog.title: Weight decay on Muon without cautious mask

backlog.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the LR decays over the final 70% of the time budget instead of 50%. Keep the linear warmdown shape and FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.0.
backlog.title: Warmdown ratio 0.7

backlog.spec: Replace the linear time-based warmdown with a cosine decay from the peak LR to FINAL_LR_FRAC over the final WARMDOWN_RATIO of the budget. Keep WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.5 and the same peak LRs.
backlog.title: Cosine warmdown shape

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so the LR ramps linearly from zero over the first 2% of the time budget before the warmdown begins. Everything else stays the same.
backlog.title: Short linear warmup

backlog.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of the model parameters with decay 0.999, updated after each optimizer step, and use the EMA weights for the final evaluation call. Do not alter the evaluation call itself; only swap the parameter values used by the model before the existing eval runs.
backlog.title: Weight EMA for evaluation

backlog.spec: Scale the effective weight decay linearly from WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.2 at the start to 0.0 at the end of the time budget, tracking the elapsed-time fraction used by the LR schedule. Apply this to the Muon and any other decayed parameter groups.
backlog.title: Weight decay linearly annealed to zero

backlog.spec: Raise WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.4 to test whether stronger regularization helps the small model over a 300 s run. Leave everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Higher weight decay

backlog.spec: Add a z-loss term of 1e-4 times the mean squared log-sum-exp of the output logits to the training loss to keep logits from drifting in scale. Apply it only to the training loss, not the evaluation.
backlog.title: Logit z-loss

backlog.spec: Apply a soft cap to the output logits with logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15) before the cross-entropy in both training and the model's forward pass. Keep the rest of the architecture unchanged.
backlog.title: Logit soft-capping

backlog.spec: Normalize queries and keys per head with RMSNorm (or an L2 norm scaled by a learnable scalar initialized to about 1/sqrt(head_dim)) just before the rotary embedding is applied. Keep attention scaling consistent with the change.
backlog.title: QK-norm on queries and keys

backlog.spec: Use the squared ReLU activation (relu(x)^2) in the MLP block in place of the current activation, keeping the MLP width and parameter count the same. Only the nonlinearity changes.
backlog.title: ReLU-squared vs GELU MLP

backlog.spec: Add a learned per-layer gate that mixes the first layer's attention value vectors into the value projection of later layers, with the mixing weight initialized to zero. This adds little compute and no extra sequence-length cost.
backlog.title: Value embeddings (ResFormer style)

backlog.spec: Add a small hashed bigram embedding table, indexed by hash(previous token, current token) modulo a table size such as 4096, and add its output to the token embedding with a learned scalar initialized at zero. Keep the main embedding dimension unchanged.
backlog.title: Bigram hash embedding

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 10 and ASPECT_RATIO = 52 so model_dim stays near the baseline width while adding two layers. Keep HEAD_DIM and the other settings the same, and check that the model still fits in memory at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64.
backlog.title: Deeper, narrower model

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 6 and ASPECT_RATIO = 85 so the width grows while depth shrinks, aiming for more throughput per step within the 300 s budget. Keep HEAD_DIM = 128 and the other settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Shallower, wider model

backlog.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "SSLL" so two of the four blocks use full context, testing whether more global attention layers help more than the extra compute costs. Keep all other settings.
backlog.title: Full attention in every layer pattern change

backlog.spec: Change the rotary embedding base from 10000 to 100000 to allow longer-range position signal in attention. Only the rotary base changes.
backlog.title: Rotary base frequency

backlog.spec: Use grouped-query attention with the number of key/value heads set to half the query heads, reducing KV projection size and memory traffic. Keep the number of query heads and model_dim unchanged, and keep the rest of the model identical.
backlog.title: Grouped-query attention with fewer KV heads

backlog.spec: Lower TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 so each step uses half as many tokens and the 300 s budget yields roughly twice as many optimizer updates. Keep the LRs unchanged and make sure gradient accumulation still divides cleanly by DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE.
backlog.title: Smaller batch for more optimizer steps

backlog.spec: Raise TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**20 using more gradient accumulation steps at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64, trading fewer updates for lower gradient noise. Keep the LRs unchanged.
backlog.title: Larger batch for stability

backlog.spec: Start training with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17 and double it at fixed fractions of the time budget (for example at 25% and 60%) up to 2**19, with gradient accumulation adjusted accordingly. Recompute the accumulation steps whenever the batch size changes and keep the LR unchanged.
backlog.title: Batch size ramp

backlog.spec: Train the first 30% of the time budget on half-length sequences and the remaining 70% on full-length sequences, keeping the number of tokens per step constant by doubling the batch rows for the short phase. This changes only how the existing batches are shaped inside the training loop.
backlog.title: Sequence length curriculum

backlog.spec: Compute the cross-entropy loss in float32 by casting the logits to float before the loss call, while keeping the rest of the forward pass in bf16 autocast. This guards against precision loss in the loss and should be near-free in compute.
backlog.title: Z-loss-free bf16 reduction check

backlog.spec: Wrap the Muon Newton-Schulz update in torch.compile so the orthogonalization kernels are fused, reducing the optimizer overhead per step. Keep the update math identical and make sure the compile does not trigger recompiles across steps.
backlog.title: Fused Muon step via torch.compile

backlog.spec: Scale the embedding initialization standard deviation to 0.5 times its current value while keeping the zero-initialized residual output projections unchanged. This adjusts the starting signal magnitude without changing the optimizer or architecture otherwise.
backlog.title: Init scale tuning

backlog.spec: Pass label_smoothing=0.05 to the cross-entropy call that computes the training loss (F.cross_entropy or equivalent). Leave the evaluation/val_bpb path untouched so the metric stays comparable. Only the training loss changes. This is a one-line regularizer that softens targets and may improve calibration and generalization within the fixed 300 s budget.
backlog.title: Label smoothing on the cross-entropy loss

backlog.spec: Before each optimizer step, call torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ over all trainable parameters with max_norm=1.0 and keep the rest of the loop unchanged. Gradients are clipped per step, which guards against occasional loss spikes at the high embedding and scalar learning rates (EMBEDDING_LR 0.6, SCALAR_LR 0.5) and could allow a more aggressive step size. Log nothing new; the metric path is untouched.
backlog.title: Global gradient-norm clipping

backlog.spec: Give each transformer block's Muon matrix parameters a learning-rate multiplier that decays with depth, for example lr_mult = 1.0 for the first block linearly down to 0.5 for the last block, applied on top of MATRIX_LR. Implement it by building separate Muon param groups per layer with scaled 'lr' values. Embeddings, lm_head and scalars keep their current learning rates. Hypothesis: deeper layers are noisier and benefit from smaller steps.
backlog.title: Depth-scaled learning rate for matrix parameters

backlog.spec: Replace the warmdown schedule for the Adam-managed parameters (token embedding, lm_head, per-layer scalars) with a schedule-free AdamW update: keep a fast iterate z that takes gradient steps and an averaged iterate x = (1-c)x + c z used for the forward pass during training and for evaluation, with c = 1/(step+1) style averaging and a constant base learning rate, no warmdown. Keep Muon for matrix parameters unchanged. The idea removes the need to tune the decay end point of the time budget.
backlog.title: Schedule-free AdamW for non-matrix parameters

backlog.spec: Change each transformer block from the sequential form x = x + attn(norm(x)); x = x + mlp(norm(x)) to the parallel form x = x + attn(norm(x)) + mlp(norm(x)), sharing one pre-attention norm for both branches. Keep the same width, depth, heads and sliding-window pattern. The parallel block reduces the number of sequential kernel launches per layer, which can raise tokens per second and therefore optimizer steps in 300 s.
backlog.title: Parallel attention and MLP residual block

backlog.spec: Keep the number of unique transformer blocks at 3 but run the stack as a loop of 2 passes over those 3 blocks (effective depth 6), so the parameter count drops by about half while compute per token stays the same. Keep per-pass learned scalars (one set per effective layer) so each pass can still differ. Preserve the window pattern by indexing the per-layer window size by effective layer index. This is a bold parameter-efficiency test: if loss holds, the freed parameter budget can be spent on a wider model.
backlog.title: Looped weight-shared transformer blocks

backlog.spec: During training only, for each transformer block after the first, skip the block's residual contribution with probability p=0.1 for that micro-batch and rescale nothing (the residual path still passes through). Evaluation uses all layers with no drop. Use a per-forward Bernoulli mask per block created with torch.rand on the device. This acts as depth regularization and also reduces average compute per step, which may add steps within the fixed time budget.
backlog.title: Stochastic layer drop during training

backlog.spec: Where the data stream contains document boundaries marked by the BOS token id, build an attention mask so that tokens cannot attend across a BOS boundary inside a packed sequence (block-diagonal causal mask per document, combined with the existing sliding-window mask). Compute the mask from the input token ids inside train.py with torch operations only; do not read prepare.py internals. Keep evaluation consistent with training. Hypothesis: packing unrelated documents into one context wastes capacity and adds noise to gradients.
backlog.title: Document-boundary-aware attention reset

backlog.spec: Insert a single learnable scalar s (initialized to 1.0, kept in the Adam scalar group with SCALAR_LR) that multiplies the final normalized hidden state before lm_head, so logits = lm_head(s * norm(h)). This lets the model adapt the softmax temperature during training instead of relying on the fixed scale produced by the head initialization and the learning rates of the output layer. No other change.
backlog.title: Learnable output logit scale

backlog.spec: With the current model (DEPTH 6, ASPECT_RATIO 85) and TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18, sweep EMBEDDING_LR down to 0.3 while keeping SCALAR_LR at 0.5 and UNEMBEDDING_LR at 0.004. Use a single run with EMBEDDING_LR=0.3 and leave all other hyperparameters fixed. The current embedding LR was set for a different model and batch size, so a lower value may improve stability and final loss. This is a cheap, low-risk tuning step.
backlog.title: Retune embedding and scalar learning rates for the smaller model

incumbent.description: Set DEPTH to 6 and ASPECT_RATIO to 85 as specified; note that model_dim rounds up to 512 (6*85=510, next multiple of HEAD_DIM 128), so width is unchanged and this effectively tests a shallower 6-layer model with the same width.

Halving TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE (slot 0, 1.0923, -0.0222) and a smaller model, DEPTH 6 with ASPECT_RATIO 85 (slot 6, 1.0683/1.0635, -0.0264, tripwire flag, so check it), were both accepted. WARMUP_RATIO 0.02 gave 1.0604/1.0620 (-0.0047) but was rejected, so it is worth rechecking against the current incumbent, since the deltas are small and noise is unmeasured. Slots 5 and 11 failed on patch errors, so retry the MATRIX_LR 0.03 and 3 Newton-Schulz ideas with exact SEARCH text.
